blockers.statement: The current daemon and gem5 bridge do not advertise or route capability bit 8 or message types 18/19/20; CP-0022 proves local codec behavior only.
Public A1 code-object and memory contracts still expose zero GPU VAs and fixture-only dispatch; coordinated mapping leases, kernarg publication, daemon-owned AQL, and completion remain for CP-0023.
The retained Triton descriptor carries 12 DWORD (48-byte) kernarg preload and native entry-offset semantics are not implemented; generic admission must reject it explicitly until CP support exists.

changes: Accepted the self-amdgpu-runtime payload-v2 generic dispatch codec and strict admission tests while preserving the v1 envelope and records.
Added opt-in capability bit 8 and reserved generic request/ack/completion records 18/19/20 with MAP_OBJECT, ALLOC_KERNARG, SUBMIT_AQL, and UNMAP_OBJECT stage validation.
Bound fixed 4096-byte big-endian records, CRC and zero-tail rules, owner-scoped id/generation identities, bounded signal/geometry/kernarg checks, and canonical failure responses.
Bound the retained Triton vecadd target, 5,408-byte HSACO, 48-byte kernarg, and 12-DWORD preload as an explicit NOT_SUPPORTED admission case.
Kept daemon routing, mapping leases, packet-visible kernarg publication, AQL construction/submission, normal launcher, simulator execution, and fallback false.
limitations: CP-0022 is a child codec/admission checkpoint. The fresh runtime build and CTest evidence do not invoke a daemon handler, gem5 bridge, normal Triton launcher, compiler/JIT, or GPU execution.
Framing remains v1 major/minor 1.0 and existing v1 records remain unchanged; payload v2.0 and bit 8 are opt-in and are not advertised by the current daemon.
MAP/ALLOC_KERNARG/SUBMIT_AQL/UNMAP validate identities and response shapes but do not allocate mappings, publish bytes, construct a packet, submit a queue, or emit completion.
The exact Triton target and descriptor metadata are hash-bound from CP-0021. Its 12-DWORD preload is an explicit NOT_SUPPORTED result; no preload-aware +256-byte entry handling is claimed.
Triton E2E, Qwen execution, timing/performance, output differential, and CPU/NVIDIA fallback remain 0/1 or false.

argv: Implement coordinated daemon/client mapping leases, packet-visible kernarg publication, preload-aware AQL submission, and normal Triton launcher handoff without CPU or NVIDIA fallback
next_action.expected: CP-0023 must connect the reviewed v2 codec to owner-bound daemon/gem5 state, map a committed code object, publish packet-visible kernarg bytes, construct and submit a daemon-owned AQL packet, and prove normal Triton vecadd behavior without CPU or NVIDIA fallback. Unsupported preload or stale ownership must fail closed.

The CP22 codec must remain the canonical validation boundary while daemon and gem5 handlers are integrated.
